title: The Kids Said the Man in the Basement Only Wants to Play #shorts #scarystories
description:
Never hide while he's counting.

Follow for a new scary story every night.

#scarystory #horrorstories #creepy #shorts

beats.text: Something under the stairs was counting out loud. And it was almost done.
In October, I babysat for the Carvers on a stormy Friday night.
Their kids, Leo and Ivy, were sweet. Polite. A little too quiet.
After dinner, Ivy asked if they could play hide and seek with the counting man.
She said he lives in the basement, and he only wants to play.
I laughed and sent them to brush their teeth.
Then my phone buzzed. It was Mrs. Carver.

overlay.message: If the kids mention the counting man, do NOT let them play.

beats.text: I texted back, asking her who that was.
She never answered.
At ten, thunder hit, and the lights went out.
From under the floor, a deep voice began to count. One. Two. Three.
I ran upstairs. Ivy was hiding under her blanket, shaking.
Leo's bed was empty.
The basement door at the end of the hall stood wide open.
The voice reached seventeen. Eighteen.
I went down with my phone light, step by creaking step.
Leo was curled inside an old wardrobe, hands over his ears.
Behind him, something tall unfolded from the dark and whispered, twenty.
Its grin stretched from ear to ear.
I grabbed Leo, ran, slammed the door, and pushed a chair against it.
The Carvers rushed home at midnight with two police officers.
The basement was empty. Just the wardrobe, and chalk marks on the wall.
Names. Dozens of children's names, each one crossed out.
Mrs. Carver finally told me. A boy vanished in that house in 1987, during a game of hide and seek.
Nobody ever found him. He's been looking for playmates ever since.
They moved out that week. I never babysat again.
But last night, in my own basement, I heard someone start counting. One. Two.
